In the draft the sentence reads "to ask questions of Mr. de Witte; but their efforts had been immense" — "their" now has no plural antecedent. The Senator asked questions of Mr. de Witte (singular), so "their efforts" is now ambiguous/broken: it could be read as the Senator and de Witte, or it is simply unmoored. The pivot "but" (Adams avoiding Berlin) is converted into a parenthetical aside, which actually parses — a reader understands he chose Sweden over Berlin. No structural damage.
